bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court Allows Ayurvedic Lecturers' Appeals Against Termination of Services Due to ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Allows Ayurvedic Lecturers' Appeals Against Termination of Services Due to Misinterpretation of Eligibility Criteria. Court Found that Eligibility Should be Assessed Based on Cutoff Date, Not Initial Appointment Date Under Bihar Private Medical (Indian System of Medicine) College (Taking over) Act, 1985. Admin 2026-10-26 02:14:50 9 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The case involved five appellants who were appointed as Lecturers in private Ayurvedic Colleges between March 14, 1978, and May 10, 1979, and later promoted to Reader/Professor. Following the enactment of the Bihar Private Medical (Indian System of Medicine) College (Taking over) Act, 1985, the State of Bihar took over management of private Ayurvedic colleges, including the Sri Dhanwantri Ayurved College. A Screening Committee was constituted to assess the qualifications of teaching staff, leading to the absorption of some employees while others, including the appellants, were terminated due to a lack of post-qualification teaching experience. The appellants challenged their termination in the High Court, which upheld the decision based on the requirement of three years of teaching experience as per the CCIM Act, 1970. The Supreme Court found that the High Court erred in assessing eligibility based on initial appointment dates rather than the cutoff date of June 1, 1986, as specified in the notification. The Court ruled that the appellants were eligible for absorption and ordered their reinstatement with consequential benefits, while also addressing the issue of superannuation for some appellants. The appeals were allowed, and the High Court's judgments were quashed. Headnote A) Administrative Law - Absorption of Employees - Eligibility Criteria - Bihar Private Medical (Indian System of Medicine) College (Taking over) Act, 1985, Section 3, 6 - The court held that the eligibility of teaching staff should be assessed based on qualifications and experience as of the cutoff date, not the date of initial appointment. The High Court's conclusion that the appellants lacked necessary experience was found to be a misconception of law (Paras 24-29). bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar School Labs Face November Deadline After Construction Slows - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar School Labs Face November Deadline After Construction Slows Breaking News Bihar School Labs Face November Deadline After Construction Slows By Tenzin Choden October 26, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar education authorities have issued show-cause notices to RailTel and Telecommunications Consultants India Ltd (TCIL) after science laboratory construction was completed in only 351 of 2,199 government secondary and higher secondary schools across the state. Both agencies have been ordered to accelerate the work and meet a November 30 deadline. The action followed a review conducted on October 24 by Navdeep Shukla, state project director of the Bihar Education Project Council. According to a department communique, RailTel had completed laboratories in 78 of the 1,055 schools assigned to it, while TCIL had completed work in 273 of the 1,144 schools allotted to it. The review also found that construction had not started in some schools. The laboratories are being established under the Samagra Shiksha scheme on a turnkey basis and are intended to provide physics, chemistry and biology facilities in government schools. Under the revised directions, RailTel must complete work in 518 schools and TCIL in 816 schools by November 30. The agencies are also required to supply furniture and equipment and hand over the completed laboratories to the respective headmasters. The education department has warned that penalties could be imposed if the agencies fail to meet the targets. TCIL has been assigned work across 20 districts, while RailTel is responsible for 18 districts. The distribution of work means that the implementation delay spans multiple administrative jurisdictions rather than being limited to a single school or district. The department has directed district education officers, district programme officers and Samagra Shiksha officials to monitor progress regularly, coordinate with the executing agencies and resolve obstacles promptly. The project director also emphasised that construction quality must be maintained while the work is expedited. Engineers have been instructed to conduct field visits to check progress and ensure that the laboratories are completed to the required standard. The directions cover not only civil construction but also the delivery of furniture and laboratory equipment before the facilities are handed over. The figures in the department’s review show that 1,848 of the 2,199 planned laboratories remained incomplete at the time of assessment. RailTel had completed roughly 7% of its assigned work, while TCIL had completed roughly 24% of its allocation. The November 30 deadline therefore requires both agencies to complete the majority of their pending assignments within the period set by the state authorities. The show-cause notices place responsibility for explaining the delay on the two executing agencies. District-level officials and engineers have been given a monitoring role as the department seeks to move the project from construction to operational handover. The next formal milestone is the November 30 completion deadline, when the agencies are expected to finish the remaining laboratories, provide the required equipment and transfer the facilities to schools. national_raw_news.title: PM Modi Inaugurates RBI’s Data Centre, Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, describing the facilities as an important step towards strengthening India’s digital infrastructure and safeguarding its financial system against emerging cyber threats. Invoking the blessings of Lord Jagannath, PM Modi said the inauguration marked a significant occasion for Odisha and the country. He congratulated the RBI and all those associated with establishing the two facilities. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister said India’s governance model was driven by the principles of pro-people, proactive and good governance, with a focus on equitable development and ensuring that opportunities reach villages and smaller towns. He highlighted the expansion of infrastructure, healthcare facilities and digital connectivity, saying that improving citizens’ lives and creating new opportunities had become central to governance. Digital Banking Expands Financial Inclusion PM Modi said India had witnessed a major transformation in financial inclusion, with digital banking connecting people across the country to round-the-clock banking services. He noted that nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts had been opened, enabling the direct transfer of government benefits to beneficiaries and helping eliminate leakages in the delivery of welfare assistance. The Prime Minister also highlighted the role of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma in expanding access to formal credit. He said small entrepreneurs, street vendors, traditional artisans and workers in the unorganised sector were now able to access loans without the need for conventional collateral. According to PM Modi, around 13 crore people had become first-time entrepreneurs under the Mudra Yojana. He also highlighted financial assistance extended to Self-Help Groups representing 10 crore rural women. He credited the RBI, commercial banks and banking employees for expanding access to financial services, including through the widespread adoption of RuPay cards. Social Security Schemes Strengthen Financial Protection The Prime Minister also underlined the contribution of social security schemes in extending financial protection to vulnerable sections of society. He said the Atal Pension Yojana covered around nine crore citizens, including 38 lakh beneficiaries in Odisha. PM Modi highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, which provides accident insurance, and the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, which offers life insurance at affordable premiums. He said insurance coverage and timely claim payments had helped families cope with financial difficulties, describing these initiatives as an example of good governance. Cybersecurity Key to Protecting India’s Financial System Emphasising the importance of the newly inaugurated facilities, PM Modi said the focus of the past decade had been on bringing the unbanked into the formal banking system, while the coming decade would concentrate on making banking more efficient, reliable and secure. He warned that modern conflicts were no longer limited to conventional weapons, as cyberattacks could also target and weaken a country’s economy. PM Modi said protecting India’s expanding financial system from cybercriminals and cyberterrorists was essential as the country strengthened its economic position. He underscored the need for modern computing infrastructure, advanced cybersecurity capabilities and specialised training to address emerging threats. The new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute are expected to strengthen the RBI’s technological infrastructure and cybersecurity preparedness. Odisha Emerging as a Growth Hub PM Modi also highlighted the growing economic potential of eastern India, describing the region as an important driver of the vision of Viksit Bharat. He said Odisha was expanding beyond its traditional mineral-based industries and developing new opportunities in semiconductors, electronics, data centres and advanced computing. The Prime Minister expressed confidence that the emerging sectors would create fresh opportunities for the state’s youth and contribute to Odisha’s economic transformation. He concluded by extending festive greetings and invoking the slogan “Jai Jagannath”. -PIB
